answer: You have 30 days from the date of discharge to submit a standard reimbursement claim [1][2]. However, for Aurora Group Health corporate plans, the submission deadline is extended to 60 days from discharge [5], whereas an archived 2024 guideline specified a 15-day limit [3].
The room rent limit on the Silver plan is 2% of the sum insured per day [3][4]. If you occupy a room exceeding this limit, proportionate deductions apply to all associated hospital charges [5].
No, maternity is not covered on the Bronze plan at any sum insured [1][2]. Maternity coverage is only available on the Silver, Gold, and Platinum plans [1].

The waiting period for pre-existing diseases is 36 months on standard retail plans, which applies to declared conditions like hypertension, diabetes, and cardiac conditions unless explicitly waived in writing [3][5]. However, under the Aurora Senior Care plan for ages 60 and above, the pre-existing disease waiting period is reduced to 24 months [5].
The grace period for an annual policy is 30 days from the renewal due date [1][5].

As of 1 April 2026, Aurora's network covers 11,400 hospitals across 780 towns [1]. Because hospitals join and leave the network continuously, the authoritative list is maintained in the Aurora app and online portal [1].

Under the Gold plan, the no-claim bonus is 25% of the base sum insured for each claim-free year, accumulating to a maximum of 100% [1][5]. If a claim is made, the accumulated bonus is not reduced; it only stops accumulating for that year [1].
No, you cannot claim for IVF treatment [1]. Infertility, assisted reproduction, and IVF are listed as permanent treatment-related exclusions [1].
The cataract surgery sub-limit on the Gold plan is ₹75,000 per eye [1].

If you are not satisfied with the Stage 1 outcome, you can escalate the matter to Aurora's Grievance Redressal Officer [2]. If Aurora's final response remains unsatisfactory or if they have not responded within 30 days of the original complaint, you may approach the Insurance Ombudsman for your region [1].

Across all plans, road ambulance cover is provided up to ₹5,000 per hospitalisation [1]. Additionally, under the Aurora Gold plan, air ambulance is covered up to ₹2,50,000 per policy year within India with prior authorisation [5].

Yes, in-patient treatment for mental illness is covered on the same terms as physical illness, as required by the Mental Healthcare Act 2017 [1]. The standard 30-day initial waiting period applies, but there is no separate waiting period for mental illness [1].

The free-look period is the window in which a new policyholder can return or cancel a new policy for a refund [2][3]. It lasts for 15 days from receiving the policy document, or 30 days if the policy was sold through distance marketing [1][2]. If cancelled during this period, the premium is refunded minus proportionate risk premium for the period of cover, medical examination costs, and stamp duty [2].
You earn 150 wellness points per year for completing an annual health check-up [1].

A day-care procedure is a procedure that requires less than 24 hours of hospitalisation due to technological advances, making it payable despite the general 24-hour admission requirement [3]. It explicitly does not include out-patient treatment [3].
For an emergency cashless admission, the hospital must notify Aurora within 24 hours of admission [1][5]. Aurora will then respond to the pre-authorisation request within 1 hour [1][2].
No, Aurora does not use a Third Party Administrator (TPA) [1]. Instead, it administers its own claims directly [1].

To qualify as a hospital under the policy, a facility must have at least 10 in-patient beds in towns with a population below 10 lakh [1]. In all other locations, it must have at least 15 in-patient beds [1].

No, not everything will be paid because the Silver plan caps room rent at 2% of the sum insured, which is ₹10,000 per day for a ₹5,00,000 policy [1][2]. Because you chose a room at ₹15,000 per day, a proportionate deduction based on an eligibility ratio of 0.667 will apply, reducing the payout on room rent and associated medical charges [1][5].

Dependent parents can be added under the Silver (at an extra premium), Gold, and Platinum plans, but are not permitted under the Bronze plan [1]. When you add a parent, your premium will be determined by the age of the eldest member covered, which often increases the policy's cost [4].
